fields.Distinctive evidence: Observed: white dimensional infrastructure tiles with blue/purple edge accents introduce a concrete GPU catalogue, comparison table and deployment-mode cards.
fields.Why it matters and strongest judgment: Interpretation: strongest reference for making infrastructure feel purchasable and understandable, although its brand is less distinctive than Aethir or Celestia. Origin, catalyst and reason for attention Unknown.
fields.Project, audience, and token role: GPU cloud for AI teams and suppliers. Official IO Coin docs describe service payments, supplier compensation and staking; customers can pay using fiat/USDC, per project documentation.
fields.Attention and buyer conversion: Savings/waitlist claims lead to Get Started and deployment routes; IO Coin/staking are footer routes. No checkout attempted; conversion outcome Unknown.
fields.Participation and return value: Public catalogue, deployment explanations and docs help non-buyers evaluate; continued compute usage is a concrete proposed return loop, operation not tested.
fields.Trust and free choice: Hardware configurations and prices expose detail, but comparator table is explicitly dated July 30, 2025. SOC2/GDPR badges, service status and savings claims were not audited.
fields.Unknowns and untested behavior: GPU availability, savings calculations, service operation, compliance claims, token payment implementation and mobile untested.
fields.Counterevidence or what would change the: Dated comparator prices and mixed per-card/cluster rates need care; the inquiry overlay interrupts browsing. A cleaner current price basis would strengthen trust.
fields.Borrowable principle, not protected expr: Show actual objects a customer can use, then organize the page around concrete actions and constraints.
fields.Avoid or no material avoid finding: Avoid copying integration logos or making unsupported availability/savings claims; do not substitute a decorated mock dashboard for a defined product.
